story: Bright stars and thick dust are scattered throughout this Hubble image of the spiral galaxy Messier 83, also known as the Southern Pinwheel Galaxy. It lies about 15 million light-years away in the constellation Hydra.

Messier 83 is a barred spiral, one with a straight band of stars across its centre from which its arms unwind, and it is among the largest and closest barred spirals to us. That combination of size and nearness makes it an appealing target, since astronomers can study its structure in fine detail.

The galaxy also holds some puzzles. Many supernova explosions, the violent deaths of stars, have gone off within it. And at its core there appears to be a double nucleus, two concentrations rather than one, a feature astronomers are still working to understand.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.52 x 4.89 arcminutes) and distance (15 million light years), the frame spans roughly 33,000 × 21,000 light-years. Its light set out about 15 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using ultraviolet, blue and visible filters. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is ultraviolet light, which the eye cannot see, and this level of detail is far beyond what an eye could make out.
